reviews.body:
**Merge decision: YES IN PRINCIPLE, but NOT READY TO MERGE THIS HEAD — strongest CPU memory improvement (reviewed 16 October 2026).**

Read the source diff and evidence at `e8f3eb8` (production code `5a6812b`). Replacing the whole corrected `Irefframes` stack with one temporary frame has a direct, physical benefit: 24-frame 3710×3838 tutorial, j4, 5×5, dose + noDW + even/odd, **peak RSS 4.388 → 3.134 GiB** (28.56–29.02% across the six measured pairs). The code preserves the float intermediate store, ascending total/even/odd accumulation, selected-frame parity and model-time offset in both polynomial and general paths; retained exact-product tests and native Linux CI are positive. The full-job wall interval crosses zero, so **do not claim a speedup**. The benefit applies to unweighted/noDW/even-odd reconstruction, not dose-only runs.

Compared with the other proposals this is relatively contained buffer-lifetime logic and does not rewrite RELION FFTs or change interpolation formulas. I favour merging this **after** the following final qualifications, not as a blanket approval of the October 14 base:
1. Rebase/compose against current `main` `d7171b8`, now including #187 FFTW plan cache/DW copy elision, #188 host THP notes and #185 report changes. Run fresh CPU-only CTests and strict full-tree exact products across global/5×5, j1/j4, dose/noDW/even-odd, binning and relevant fallback paths; retain complete inventory including temporary artifacts. #182's baseline-side truncated temporary is *not* proof of a #178 defect but remains unresolved for its own strict tutorial case.
2. Run matched cpu64 full-geometry wall/RSS with the **same** declared THP policy on both arms (including the release-recommended glibc setting where applicable); validate combined memory peak rather than adding old #178/#187 RSS deltas.
3. Confirm native CUDA build and the actual CPU fallback in a supported configuration, especially the borrowed input/one-frame scratch lifetime, without claiming native GPU testing from CUDA compilation.

**Disposition:** priority integration candidate, request the minimal current-main qualification PR/delta, then merge if exactness and material RSS gain remain. Do **not** pull in stacked #182: its fusion trial does not justify added code.

Reviewer: Sonnet 5.5

Needs a rebase, then merge-ready on correctness: the change is exact as far as I can establish and the RSS claim follows from the code. It conflicts with main d7171b81 mechanically, and the 28.6-29.0% saving should be re-measured on current main before merge.

1. P1 `src/motioncorr_runner.cpp:2083` (merge conflict, mechanical). #195 added `NativeS16MovieStaging s16_staging; NativeS8MovieStaging s8_staging;` on the lines next to the `Irefframes` declaration this PR deletes. Resolution: keep the two staging lines, drop `Irefframes`. Nothing else on main references `Irefframes`, and #187/#195/#196/#197 do not touch the unweighted fallback block. I resolved it in a throwaway worktree on d7171b81: it builds and `CpuUnweightedStream` passes (macOS CPU-only, so the allocation witness is not compiled; see item 4).
2. P2 Re-measure on d7171b81. The saving follows from the code: median peak difference 1,335,028 KiB vs 3710x3838x4x24 = 1,334,904 KiB (0.01%), so the stack is live at the baseline peak and the one-frame scratch is already freed by then. #187 removes a DW iFFT copy, and the candidate's 3.13 GiB peak may now be set by another stage, so the gain on main may be smaller. Run the tutorial dose+noDW+even/odd j4 pair on the same THP policy for both arms.
3. P2 `docs/cpu_stream_20261014/*/results.json`: every end-to-end run has an even frame count (tutorial 24, synthetic 16). Odd-frame parity (`iframe % 2` in `sumUnweightedFrames`) is covered only by the kernel test (7 frames, `tests/test_cpu_unweighted_stream.cpp`). The code is right (parity uses the selected-frame index in both old and new), but add one odd-frame end-to-end tree (even/odd + `--bin_factor 2`) to the post-rebase matrix.
4. P3 `tests/test_cpu_unweighted_stream.cpp:143-145,160`: without `MOTIONCORR_ALLOCATION_WITNESS` (all non-Linux builds) the one-frame bound is never checked, yet the test still prints "...scratch bound PASS". Print "bound not witnessed" in that case. Linux CI log line 976 shows it was witnessed there, including the N-frame control.
5. Strict-tree failure (`.tutorial_noDW.mrc.128xfS`, 46,661,632 B): not in this PR's evidence and not a product bug that I can find. All 35 comparisons in `{tutorial,synthetic}-*/results.json` have empty `only_a`/`only_b`/`problems`. The file is reported in #182/#177 on the baseline (main binary) side only. Neither binary can create that name: MRC products are written in place at the final name (`Image::write`, `src/image.h:332`; `submitImageWrite`, `src/motioncorr_runner.cpp:1527`); the only temp-then-rename writers are STAR (`metadata_table.cpp:1529,2229`, suffix `.tmp`). A dot-prefixed name with a 6-character random suffix is rsync's partial-file name, and the size is ~82% of the 56,956,944 B complete noDW file with a valid header. I infer a harness copy/sync artefact. This is unproven; to settle it, check how the output tree reached the comparison host, and re-run the tutorial pair.

Verified: the production diff is `5a6812b` only (nothing outside `docs/cpu_stream_20261014/` changes between `5a6812b` and `e8f3eb8`, and the tree `64057a8` matches `ci-status.json`). Float store per frame, ascending total/even/odd order, `iframe + frame_offset` model time (int square preserved), alias non-ownership, and no OpenMP sharing of the scratch hold on read. Recomputed from the retained JSON: 35/35 clean comparisons, all RSS ranges and wall medians match the PR body. Not checked: native CUDA execution, the unpublished measurement commit `c9dbe595` (only its tree id), any end-to-end run of my own, cpu64/4GPUs.

Next action: rebase onto d7171b81 per item 1, re-run the tutorial RSS/wall pair and a strict-tree check (include one odd-frame case) on the merged head, then mark ready.
